title: I Followed the Hardware-Store Rain Check Into Corporate Chat

parts.text: I asked for a rain check on sale paint at 10:12 because the endcap was empty. The clerk, Daryl, said rain checks were a myth. I was forty-four, holding the ad that said rain checks available. I asked for a manager. Daryl was the manager. I filled the paper form from the website PDF on my phone anyway and left it at the desk. Saturday the paint was back at full price. Daryl shrugged. Then corporate's mystery shopper — a woman with a clipboard I recognized from a training poster — asked Daryl if he honored rain checks.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The clipboard from the training poster is about to hear him call rain checks a myth.

social.video_title: He called rain checks a myth in front of the ad — Part 1/2
social.description: Empty endcap, website PDF, full price Saturday. Then a clipboard. Would you have driven to another store?

parts.text: I said I had left a form. They found it under a coupon pile. I got the sale price and a rain-check number that exists. Daryl learned the word myth is expensive. I painted a bathroom the color of less nonsense. The ad was true. Paper under coupons is still paper. Corporate chat did not need me after the clipboard, but I still have the PDF.

social.video_title: They found my form under the coupons — Part 2/2
social.description: Sale price honored, bathroom painted, myth retired. Was an ad a rumor?
